description.text: Luigi Pirandello was born in 1867 in the Sicilian town of Agrigento, where his family’s mercantile background and the region’s rich cultural heritage shaped his early life and literary sensibilities.
He rose to international acclaim as a playwright and novelist, earning the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1934 for his innovative contributions to drama and his exploration of identity and perception.

curiosities.text: Pirandello’s novel *Il fu Mattia Pascal* (1904) was adapted into several films, including a 1926 silent version by Marcel L'Herbier and a 1937 adaptation by Pierre Chenal.
Despite his literary success, Pirandello’s personal life was marked by the mental illness of his wife, which influenced his later interest in psychoanalysis and the psychology of the self.
He was a member of the Italian Fascist Party, joining in 1924, though his relationship with the regime was complex and often ambivalent.
